reason: Conversation 2 asked what the smell was and where it came from, then used the answers (warm browned cooker switch, flicker, crackle) to identify an overheating supply connection. It told the customer to isolate at the consumer unit, not to touch the discoloured switch, to call 999 if it worsens, and to book an electrician who can pull the cooker out safely, all within the expected safety boundary. Conversation 1 gave only a generic stop-use warning and an appliance engineer referral, with no diagnosis, no question about the smell, and no guidance on isolation or the right trade, so it served the homeowner far less well.
